To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of anomalies in the final programs of an algorithmic learning procedure can be helpful in succinctifying those programs, and that the presence of these anomalies does not necessarily imply that those programs will be less reliable.
(1) anomalies can be used as a tool for succinctness and (2) the use of anomalies in learning can be more constructive than the use of nonanomalous learning.

(1) allowing a bounded number anomalies in the final programs produced by a learning algorithm can considerably “succintify” those final program and (2) the presence of anomalies can be useful for succinctification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: What is the most succinct way in which one can describe a finite set?

the question of how much information about a finite set of objects is needed to learn its characteristic function, and the question of what is the smallest amount of information that suffices for learning the characteristic function of a finite set of a given cardinality.
a new approach to succinct coding of finite sets and with its application to the study of the learnability of decision rules for finite sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the contexts considered, allowing a bounded number (depending on the context) of anomalies can considerably “succintify” those contexts.
, in certain infinite subclasses of characteristic functions of sets, the learning of decision procedures for sets is more succinct when anomalies are allowed.
, in the presence of anomalies, learning can be considerably more succinct than learning without anomalies, but only in certain robust contexts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
allowing a bounded (or unbounded) number of anomalies in the final learned programs does not hurt learnability and can even help succinctness.

, in certain infinite subclasses of characteristic functions of sets, the learning algorithms can learn the characteristic functions with bounded errors, but in certain other infinite subclasses, the algorithms can learn the functions exactly.
allowing a finite number of mistakes can considerably “succintify” the final programs produced by certain learning algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the notion of succinctness of a program can be extended to the notion of succinctification of a learning procedure, which can be viewed as a generalization of the notion of succinct coding of a set of data.
allowing for anomalies is an efficient means to learn succinct programs.
, in certain learning scenarios, allowing a bounded number anomalies in the final programs can be a good thing.
